title: Rational Hom adjunction and agreement of localized purity families
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Write $\mathcal C_T(\Lambda)=\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ for the bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale condensed-module category [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $F_{f,\Lambda}=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$, $G_{f,\Lambda}=f^!_\Lambda$ with its specified restricted adjunction $F_{f,\Lambda}\dashv G_{f,\Lambda}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda}$ [sk-thm-existence], and $J_{f,\Lambda}=f^*_\Lambda(-)(d)[2d]$ with the Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Use the completed integral coefficient sheaves and scalar localization $Q_T(K_0)=K_0[1/\ell]=E_T\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}K_0$ with the condensed Hom comparisons and functor comparisons of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom]; in particular every rational constructible object has an integral representative. Fix the tower adjunction $F_{f,\mathcal O_E}\dashv H_{f,E}$ and its actual purity isomorphism $\gamma^H:J_{f,\mathcal O_E}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f,E}$ [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Let $\alpha_0$ be its $\mathcal O_E$-linear Hom bijection followed by postcomposition with $(\gamma^H)^{-1}$, and put $t_0=\varepsilon^H\circ F_{f,\mathcal O_E}(\gamma^H)$. Use the fixed family $\gamma^T_E=\delta_E\gamma^H$ and its trace-transpose identification [lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison].

There is a natural $E$-linear adjunction bijection $\alpha_E:\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,E}M,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,J_{f,E}K)$ whose value for $M=Q_XM_0$, $K=Q_YK_0$ is exactly the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,E}Q_XM_0,Q_YK_0)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,\mathcal O_E}M_0,K_0)\otimes E\xrightarrow{\alpha_0\otimes1}\operatorname{Hom}(M_0,J_{f,\mathcal O_E}K_0)\otimes E\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Q_XM_0,J_{f,E}Q_YK_0).$$
This bijection is independent of the representatives, is natural also for fractional arrows $h/\ell^s$, and has counit the image of $t_0$ under the displayed compact-support and source comparisons. For the counit-preserving comparison with $G_{f,E}$ its purity map on $Q_YK_0$ is $Q_X(\gamma^T_{E,K_0})$, and hence equals the specified rational family of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. It has the trace, composition and Cartesian base-change equations of [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence]. The coefficient comparisons of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension] intertwine these very Hom bijections, units and counits for $E\subset F$, transitively for three-field chains. Affine-line integration is the localization of its integral normalization. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes the $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$ cases.

source.note: Agent interface lemma extracted from the returned 13-step proof; the full argument assigned to this node is retained verbatim in report.md.

proof.text: Write $F_0=F_{f,\mathcal O_E}$ and $J_0=J_{f,\mathcal O_E}$. The realized integral adjunction and its actual isomorphism $\gamma^H$ are supplied by [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Postcomposing its Hom bijection with $(\gamma^H)^{-1}$ gives the specified $\alpha_0$. Its inverse is explicitly $b\mapsto t_{0,K_0}\circ F_0(b)$: the inverse tower transpose is $c\mapsto\varepsilon^H_{K_0}\circ F_0(c)$ and $c=\gamma^H_{K_0}\circ b$. In particular $\alpha_0(t_{0,K_0})=1_{J_0K_0}$. Thus this is the integral adjunction with this counit, rather than an arbitrary bijection of the same Hom sets. It is $\mathcal O_E$-linear: $\alpha_0^{-1}(b)=t_{0,K_0}\circ F_0(b)$ and $F_0=R\bar f_*\circ j_!$ is $\mathcal O_E$-linear on Hom modules, since a scalar $\lambda\in\mathcal O_E$ acts on every object by the natural endomorphism $\lambda\cdot1$ of the identity of $\mathcal O_{E}$-module sheaves, which the additive functors $j_!$, $\bar f_*$ and their derived functors preserve; so $\alpha_0^{-1}$, and hence its inverse $\alpha_0$, is $\mathcal O_E$-linear and $\alpha_0\otimes1$ is defined.

source.place: Step 5, integral explicit adjoint before rationalization

proof.text: For $M=Q_XM_0$, $K=Q_YK_0$, use the two natural Hom isomorphisms and the $F$ and pullback comparisons in [det-sp-rational-localized-hom]. The twist of a rational representative is the localized integral twist by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]; the Hom comparison with $q=2d$ supplies the shift comparison. Define $\alpha_E$ by their composite with $\alpha_0\otimes1$, exactly as displayed in the statement. Tensoring $\alpha_0^{-1}$ gives its inverse, since the two composite identities are the tensor images of $\alpha_0^{-1}\alpha_0=1$ and $\alpha_0\alpha_0^{-1}=1$. In particular the result is an $E$-linear bijection, not just an injective map. Every object has a representative by the same Hom-localization node. The integral representatives lie in the required finite-Tor domain by [lem-pur-rational-lattice-adic-domain]; we do not identify an arbitrary incomplete integral module with an object of that domain.

source.place: Step 3, localized Hom formula on integral representatives

proof.text: Here is the naturality and representative check. Suppress the specified functor comparisons in formulas only. For integral arrows $a:M'_0\to M_0$, $b:K_0\to K'_0$, $u:F_0M_0\to K_0$, integral naturality gives $\alpha_0(b\circ u\circ F_0a)=J_0b\circ\alpha_0(u)\circ a$. Every element of an integral Hom tensored with $E=\mathcal O_E[1/\ell]$ is a finite sum of tensors $h_i\otimes(c_i/\ell^{s_i})$, hence is $Q(h)/\ell^s$ after choosing $s=\max s_i$ and $h=\sum_i\ell^{s-s_i}c_ih_i$. The Hom comparison identifies this with every rational arrow between representatives. By bilinearity, for $a/\ell^r$, $b/\ell^s$, $u/\ell^t$ the preceding naturality identity is divided by $\ell^{r+s+t}$. This proves naturality for all rational arrows. If $i:Q_XM_0\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XM'_0$ and $j:Q_YK_0\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YK'_0$ identify two choices of representatives, it gives $\alpha'_{E}(j\circ u\circ F_E(i^{-1}))=J_E(j)\circ\alpha_E(u)\circ i^{-1}$. This is precisely equality after transporting the two Hom sets. Two successive changes give the same equation for their composites; taking identity identifications proves independence on the fixed rational objects. All computations occur in the tensor Hom modules, so different fractions for one arrow give the same value, including when integral Hom has torsion. The existence and naturality of the comparisons used here are those of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom].

source.place: Step 3, independence of lattices and naturality for fractional arrows

proof.text: A natural Hom bijection is the adjunction $F_E\dashv J_E$. Evaluate its inverse at $1_{J_EQ_YK_0}$: by Step 1 and the identity-preserving comparisons, its counit is $Q_Y(t_{0,K_0})$, with source $F_EJ_EQ_YK_0$ identified with $Q_YF_0J_0K_0$. Its unit is likewise $Q_X(\alpha_0(1_{F_0M_0}))$ with the source and target comparisons. More explicitly, $\alpha_E(u)=J_E(u)\circ\eta_{E,M}$ and $\alpha_E^{-1}(v)=t_{E,K}\circ F_E(v)$ by naturality and evaluation at identities. The two inverse identities then say $t_{E,F_EM}\circ F_E(\eta_{E,M})=1_{F_EM}$ and $J_E(t_{E,K})\circ\eta_{E,J_EK}=1_{J_EK}$, proving the triangles. The comparisons and their naturality are exactly [det-sp-rational-localized-hom].

source.place: Step 5, unit, counit and triangles of the localized explicit adjunction

proof.text: Compare this right adjoint with the specified $G_{f,E}$, whose restricted adjunction is [sk-thm-existence]. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] its comparison $\gamma_E:J_E\to G_{f,E}$ is the unique family solving $\varepsilon_{f,E,K}\circ F_E(\gamma_{E,K})=t_{E,K}$. Integrally the counit-preserving equation for $\delta_E$ gives $\varepsilon_{f,\mathcal O_E,K_0}\circ F_0(\delta_{E,K_0}\gamma^H_{K_0})=\varepsilon^H_{K_0}\circ F_0(\gamma^H_{K_0})=t_{0,K_0}$. Under the canonical source and counit-preserving target identifications fixed in [lem-pur-tower-trace-purity-comparison], its image is $\varepsilon_{f,E,Q_YK_0}\circ F_E(Q_X\gamma^T_{E,K_0})=t_{E,Q_YK_0}$. Uniqueness therefore gives $\gamma_{E,Q_YK_0}=Q_X(\gamma^T_{E,K_0})$. The last assertion of that comparison node identifies this very map with the specified rational family. Consequently [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence] supplies its trace, composition and Cartesian base-change equations. This uses the stated comparison of actual families, not equality inferred merely from separate finite evaluations of a general derived map.

source.place: Steps 3 and 5, agreement with the specified rational family and counit

proof.text:
For $E\subset F$ let $C=C_{F/E}$ and denote the comparison maps of [sk-lem-sp-field-extension] by $b:CF_E\xrightarrow{\sim}F_FC$ and $a:CJ_E\xrightarrow{\sim}J_FC$. That node refers explicitly to the adjunction obtained by localizing the integral adjunction of [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], and states preservation of its unit and counit. That adjunction lives on the raw scalar localization, whose Hom modules are $\operatorname{Hom}(M_0,N_0)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ and whose Hom bijection is $\alpha_0\otimes1$. The natural comparison $h\otimes e\mapsto e\,h[1/\ell]$ of [det-sp-rational-localized-hom] is bijective and every condensed rational object is a localized representative, so it is an equivalence from the raw localization to $\mathcal C_T(E)$ compatible with $F$ and pullback by the same node's comparisons; Step 2 defined $\alpha_E$ as $\alpha_0\otimes1$ conjugated by exactly these comparisons. Hence under this equivalence that adjunction is the one of Steps 1--4, with the same unit and counit, and $a,b$ and $C$ are transported along it. For $u:F_EM\to K$, its extension on the left Hom set is $C(u)\circ b_M^{-1}$. Expanding $\alpha(u)=J(u)\circ\eta$ and using naturality of $a$ gives
$$\alpha_F(C(u)\circ b_M^{-1})=a_K\circ C(\alpha_E(u)).$$
Indeed the extended unit is $J_F(b_M^{-1})\circ a_{F_EM}\circ C(\eta_{E,M})$, and substitution gives the equality. Thus it is these particular Hom bijections that are intertwined. The inverse equality follows by their bijectivity, so also gives the counit square. For $E\subset F\subset L$ the comparison node states that $a$ and $b$ compose under the scalar associators. Substitution in this formula proves transitivity for the Hom bijections as well; no assertion that Hom scalar extension itself is surjective is needed.

source.place: Step 3, finite coefficient-field transitions and the unit/counit normalization

proof.text: Finally [lem-pur-transport-integral-counit-realization] identifies the actual integral counit $t_0$ with the realization of the normalized chart counits (fibre sum and iterated projective-line integration). On the affine-line projection its integration is therefore the integral normalization specified there. Step 4 sends precisely $t_0$ to $t_E$; evaluating at the coefficient unit proves that rational affine-line integration is its scalar localization, with the same twist and shift comparisons. No new normalization is chosen. All steps allow $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, where $\mathcal O_E=\mathbf Z_\ell$, giving the two final cases.
